summary.headline: Quess Q4 FY26 EBITDA rose 28% YoY to INR 86 crore at a 2.2% margin on 6% revenue growth; FY26 margin crossed 2%.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue was INR 3,892 crore (+6% YoY) with EBITDA of INR 86 crore (+28% YoY, +8% QoQ) and margin up 37 bps to 2.2%. Reported PAT was INR 64 crore, and management said adjusted PAT was stable QoQ. FY26 revenue was INR 15,305 crore (+2%), EBITDA INR 312 crore (+19%), and adjusted PAT INR 250 crore (+10%), with ROE of 20%. Management framed the year as margin-led, with high-margin Professional Staffing and Overseas now contributing about 50% of operating profitability. The Board approved a final dividend of INR 3 and a special dividend of INR 3 per share.

segments.name: General Staffing
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR 3,328 crore (+6% YoY, QoQ dip from one-time Labor Code pass-throughs in Q3); Q4 EBITDA INR 52 crore (+21% YoY), margin about 1.5%. FY26 revenue INR 13,176 crore (86% of total) and EBITDA INR 189 crore. DSO 24 days including unbilled revenue; Collect & Pay mix 76%.

segments.name: Professional Staffing
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR 232 crore; Q4 EBITDA INR 30 crore (+47% YoY), margin about 12-13%. FY26 revenue INR 930 crore (+13%) and EBITDA INR 111 crore (+43%). GCCs are about 71% of headcount deployment.

segments.name: Overseas
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR 332 crore (+16% YoY); Q4 EBITDA INR 21 crore (+18% YoY per slide, +28% per CEO), margin above 6%. FY26 revenue INR 1,197 crore (+5%) and EBITDA INR 77 crore (+21%). Middle East margin 11%, Philippines 10%, Singapore about 5.5%, Malaysia 4.3%.

guidance_outlook: Overall margin: management said 2% is now a baseline, with about 2% in the immediate term and about 2.4% over a three-year medium term; General Staffing's low margin is a drag.
Professional Staffing margin to be measured in the 11-12% range over the medium term.
Overseas blended margin target of above 6%.
General Staffing: management expects FY27 headcount growth of 10-11% and revenue growth of 12-13% for Professional Staffing.
Effective tax rate guided at 7-10% for modelling; no 80JJAA impact expected as the company continues to avail the exemption.
Labor Code: full client confirmation on revised terms expected by Q1 and most likely by end of Q2 FY27 before the P&L impact is taken.
capex_capacity: General Staffing sourcing capacity is installed for up to 50,000 people per quarter; the last two quarters delivered 37,000 and 38,000.
FY26 net headcount addition in General Staffing was about 26,000 (about 19,000 like-for-like after a 7,000-resource milestone project was exited), against a historical 45,000-50,000 average.
Sales team can deliver 275-300 new logos per year; the company added 281 new contracts in FY26 (59 in Q4).
Headcount: Professional Staffing added about 400 net billable associates in FY26, roughly 50% from the 61 new logos.
Digital platforms remain investment-focused with AI; company is building a blue-collar marketplace and AI-driven recruitment platform over a three-year plan.
demand_pricing: Professional Staffing demand mix shifted: AI, data, cloud and cyber now about 60% of demand (vs 30% two years ago); GCCs about 71% of the book, IT-in-enterprise about 20%, IT services 9-10%.

Professional Staffing revenue was INR 224 crore in one quarter (down from INR 244 crore after a one-year MSP project ended), recovering to INR 232 crore in Q4; management attributed weak YoY growth in Q3/Q4 to furlough and lower working days (T&M model).
Overseas Q4 revenue jump of INR 42 crore QoQ: about INR 10 crore one-time pass-through, remainder from organic growth, new customers and FX gains.
Middle East: record Q4 revenue, collections about 172%, more than 2,200 contractors; customers mainly in essential services (technology, insurance, telecom, e-commerce, logistics, banking, retail).
General Staffing: BFSI and CRT saw near-term softness, offset by manufacturing and infrastructure/construction demand. Like-for-like growth ex the prior-year BFSI-led decline was about 10%.
Discontinued project: about 7,000 resources and about INR 200 crore revenue (about 1.3%), milestone-based; now closed, with no other known exits flagged.

qa_highlights.question: What drove Overseas Q4 growth and is it sustainable; how is Middle East exposed to geopolitical risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the INR 42 crore QoQ revenue jump mainly to organic growth, new customers and FX gains, with about INR 10 crore one-time pass-through. Middle East closed at a record revenue and crossed AOP targets; the company is monitoring the situation closely.

qa_highlights.question: What drove General Staffing margin improvement and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said General Staffing margin is 1.5%, with focus on higher-margin customers in construction, value-added services and manufacturing, and a value-plus-volume strategy over the next four years.

qa_highlights.question: Will Professional Staffing margins go higher, and what is the blended margin path?
qa_highlights.answer: Professional Staffing margin is guided at 11-12% medium term; blended company margin 2% now, about 2.4% over three years. The shift away from 0-3 year experience roles and toward GCCs drove the gain.

qa_highlights.question: Why are Professional Staffing revenue growth and exit rate tapering, and when does growth return?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed furlough, fewer working days in Q3/Q4 and a one-year MSP project ending; 61 new logos are mostly GCCs, and management expects 12-13% revenue and 10-11% headcount growth this year.

qa_highlights.question: How much General Staffing headcount capacity is converting into revenue growth, and what share of clients accepted Labor Code revised terms?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said installed capacity is used at about 50%; FY26 like-for-like net adds were 19,000. Client confirmations on Labor Code terms are expected by Q1 and most likely by end of Q2 FY27; no percentage was given.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable is Professional Staffing margin versus peers, and is there slowdown risk from AI and GCC hiring?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Professional Staffing EBITDA was about 4.7% in FY21 and reached about 12% after five years of portfolio rebalancing. Kapil Joshi said demand is moving to 4+ year experience roles in AI, cloud and cyber, and Q4 was hit by the lowest working days.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ETR and contingent liability outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: ETR guided at 7-10%. The 80JJAA exemption is still availed (industry litigation, sub judice); GST litigation involving about 10 insurers is slow to conclude, and the company expects no change in its contingent liability position this year.

risks_watch: Labor Code: client confirmations on revised terms pending until end of Q2 FY27; P&L impact not yet taken.
General Staffing revenue growth remains muted at about 2% reported; capacity use is only about 50% and sourcing delivery was 37,000-38,000 per quarter against a 50,000 capacity.
Middle East geopolitical situation; management said it is watching closely.
Professional Staffing growth exit weakness and possible GCC/AI-led hiring slowdown, though management expects double-digit headcount growth.
GST litigation with about 10 insurers involved; contingent liability unchanged until final resolution.
summary.management_tone: Confident on margins and cash flow, with clear medium-term targets; more cautious on General Staffing volume growth, Labor Code impacts and Middle East. Management repeatedly stressed that Q3/Q4 Professional Staffing revenue was affected by calendar and furlough effects, and it gave few hard numbers on the Labor Code impact.

Importantly, our EBITDA -to-operating cash flow conversion remains strong at 80%, highlighting the disciplined working capital management and high-quality earnings.
